subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should unconfigured Docker sandboxes receive a default `pidsLimit` of 1024, and what validated opt-out should existing users have after upgrade?
rationale: This is a sandbox security hardening change, but it intentionally changes the default runtime limits for existing unconfigured deployments and the current config schema/docs do not agree on an opt-out.

options.title: Require aligned opt-out before merge
options.body: Approve the default cap direction only if the PR also documents and validates the opt-out/override path, adds focused tests, and includes real Docker proof.

options.title: Accept the hardening risk as-is
options.body: Merge the 1024 default without waiting for a broader compatibility contract, explicitly owning that some upgraded workloads may need manual config changes.

options.title: Replace this PR
options.body: Close or pause this branch and keep the canonical issue open for a maintainer-owned sandbox hardening patch.

recommendation.title: Require aligned opt-out before merge
recommendation.body: Approve the default cap direction only if the PR also documents and validates the opt-out/override path, adds focused tests, and includes real Docker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a sandbox security/default policy choice, and steipete has the strongest history signal on recent sandbox hardening plus CODEOWNERS-adjacent security routing.
